title: Duchy of Silesia
capsule: The Duchy of Silesia was created in 1139 when the Polish High Duke Bolesław III Wrymouth's inheritance was divided among his sons, giving the region to Władysław II 'the Exile'; it then fragmented further into numerous sub-duchies over the following century as the Piast dynasty multiplied. Silesia became a major site of German colonization (Ostsiedlung) from the mid-twelfth century onward, and its dukes increasingly oriented toward the Bohemian Crown. Wenceslaus II of Bohemia obtained suzerainty over most of the Silesian duchies by 1289–1291, and the region became formally part of the Bohemian Crown after the death of Přemysl II in 1305, ending its existence as a notionally separate Polish Piast polity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The original unified Duchy of Silesia's extent (modern Silesia) is well-established, but because it fragmented into dozens of sub-duchies after c. 1200, mapping it as a single entity after that point is a simplification.
